extracted.intended_audience: librarians, academic administrators, and humanities & social sciences scholars
extracted.subtask_description: Develop and implement measures for assessing scholarship in the humanities and social sciences that embody humane values and reflect disciplinary modes of inquiry; includes recognizing hidden scholarly labor and advising institutions on metric use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measures should embody humane values
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures for assessing scholarship should embody humane values like equity, openness, collegiality, quality, and community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The initiative asks what it would look like if measures reflected these humane values rather than solely quantitative proxies; those values are the core desiderata for any new metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Align metrics with humanities and social sciences modes of inquiry
rubrics_metrics.description: New methods for assessing scholarship should be appropriate to the humanities and social sciences instead of being based on the practices of more scientifically oriented scholarship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page highlights that standardized metrics based on scientific practices are misaligned with HSS scholarship and that HuMetricsHSS aims to create methods that reflect HSS disciplinary practices and values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize and reward hidden scholarly labor
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment should expose, highlight, and recognize important but often hidden scholarly work such as peer review, syllabus development, conference organizing, and mentoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HuMetricsHSS explicitly names these activities as examples of valuable scholarship that current metrics overlook and that should be incorporated into measures of scholarly contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create a values-based framework for the scholarly life well-lived
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop and support a values-based framework for understanding and evaluating all aspects of the 'scholarly life well-lived' and for promoting the nurturing of these values in scholarly practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the initiative's overarching standard: measures should not just count outputs but frame evaluation around thriving scholarly practices and cultivated values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess institutional use of metrics in context
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate how institutions use metrics in the humanities and social sciences as part of developing and implementing values-based measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HuMetricsHSS planned onsite workshops and visits (e.g., Big Ten Academic Alliance campuses) to learn from librarians and administrators how metrics are currently used, implying that assessment design should be informed by institutional practices and contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure impact that reflects disciplinary values and inquiry
rubrics_metrics.description: Impact measures should reflect the values and modes of inquiry in HSS fields rather than generic or improperly tailored impact metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted guidance from a co-investigator frames this as a critical component: designing impact measurement that mirrors HSS values and inquiry methods.
